findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the multi-word AC greps wrap-tolerant: either forbid wrapping inside the asserted phrases, or join the §I1 range before grepping (e.g. pipe through `tr '\n' ' '`).
evidence: "Replacement text (verbatim, modulo line wrapping)"
"sed -n '/^### I1/,/^### I2/p' docs/concurrency.md | grep -c 'it is implemented'` prints 1"
"the §I1 range contains `625 MiB` and `108 MiB`"
findings.finding: The plan allows the replacement text to be committed 'verbatim, modulo line wrapping', but several AC proofs grep for multi-word phrases on a single line. If wrapping falls inside a phrase, the AC fails even though the content is correct. Examples are `grep -c 'it is implemented'` (which must also print exactly 1), `grows with write volume`, `Inbound — background sync`, `625 MiB` and `108 MiB`.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — §I1 implemented / Inbound pointer / pack figures / grows-with-write-volume ACs; 'Replacement text (verbatim, modulo line wrapping)'
scenarios: The implementer wraps at ~80 columns and 'it is' ends one line while 'implemented.**' starts the next. The grep prints 0 and the AC fails on correct content.
'625' and 'MiB' land on separate lines, so the fake-remote AC fails spuriously, or the implementer awkwardly re-wraps the prose to satisfy grep.
findings.suggested_fix: For each phrase-based AC, run the check on the joined §I1 range: `sed -n '/^### I1/,/^### I2/p' docs/concurrency.md | tr '\n' ' ' | grep -o 'it is implemented' | wc -l` (expect 1). Alternatively, add a sentence saying line breaks must not fall inside any phrase an AC asserts.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make phrase greps wrap-insensitive by joining lines before matching (or require that each phrase stays on one line), and confirm the removal greps print ≥1 on origin/main before the edit.
evidence: "Replacement text (verbatim, modulo line wrapping)"

The original paragraph spans lines 61-79, so it is already hard-wrapped and old phrases may be split across lines.
findings.finding: Multi-word grep proofs are fragile because the replacement text is inserted 'modulo line wrapping'. A wrap inside a phrase makes the positive checks print 0 even though the text is present. The negative checks can also pass vacuously, because the old wrapped paragraph may already split those phrases across lines. Affected positive phrases: 'it is implemented', 'grows with write volume', 'Inbound — background sync', '625 MiB', '108 MiB', '122,794 KiB'. Affected negative phrases: 'is specified by **ADR 0106**', 'the pack the CI budget guards is blobless'.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — grep-based proofs; What changes ('verbatim, modulo line wrapping')
scenarios: The executor wraps at ~80 columns and 'it is' lands at the end of one line, 'implemented' at the start of the next: the AC prints 0 and the executor wrongly concludes the edit failed.
The old text has 'is specified by' on line 63 and '**ADR 0106**' on line 64: the removal check prints 0 on unmodified main, so it proves nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Define S="$(sed -n '/^### I1/,/^### I2/p' docs/concurrency.md | tr '\n' ' ' | tr -s ' ')" and assert each phrase with `grep -cF` against "$S". Use the same joined form for the two negative checks. Add a precondition that each negative check prints ≥1 on origin/main 9d10232dd89, so it is shown to detect the old text.
